1021.event_title: Mary McLeod Bethune opens her school with $1.50
1021.event: Mary McLeod Bethune, the daughter of formerly enslaved parents, opened the Daytona Literary and Industrial Training School for Negro Girls in a rented house with $1.50, five girls and her own son. She raised money tirelessly to keep it going, and within a few years it had grown to some 250 students; it later merged with the Cookman Institute to become Bethune-Cookman.
1021.explanation: Bethune built a lasting institution for her community from almost nothing through unceasing personal labour.
1021.tie_back: The kural ranks above all other greatness the vow never to rest one's hands from raising one's people, and Bethune's school embodies that vow.
1021._accuracy_note: A strong picture of untiring work to raise a community, read in the wider sense of kudi that some commentators allow.

1022.event_title: Kongo Gumi, the temple builders who lasted fourteen centuries
1022.event: Kongo Gumi, a temple-building firm traditionally founded in 578 by a craftsman brought from the Korean kingdom of Baekje to build the Shitennoji temple, was run by his descendants for some forty generations and is widely cited as the world's oldest continuously operating company. Temple construction still provided about 80 per cent of its revenue in 2004, but in 2006 heavy debts ended its independence as a family business.
1022.explanation: The firm's long life rested on generations of skilled craft knowledge joined to steady, unbroken work.
1022.tie_back: The kural says a family lengthens through long, sustained effort combined with full knowledge, and Kongo Gumi's fourteen centuries are an extraordinary example.
1022._accuracy_note: A close fit for knowledge plus long effort making a family line endure; the earliest centuries rest on tradition rather than surviving records.

1023.event_title: Mary Anning's family finds the first complete ichthyosaur
1023.event: After cabinetmaker Richard Anning died in 1810 leaving his family poor and in debt, his children Mary and Joseph kept collecting and selling fossils from the cliffs to support the household. In 1811 Joseph found a large fossil skull, and Mary later uncovered the rest of the skeleton; the specimen, recognised as an ichthyosaur, sold for 23 pounds and helped the family out of debt.
1023.explanation: The find launched Mary Anning's career as one of the most important fossil collectors in the history of palaeontology.
1023.tie_back: The kural promises that when someone resolves to raise the family, fortune itself girds up and runs ahead to help, and the Annings' striking find came while they were working to keep their family afloat.
1023._accuracy_note: A good illustration of good fortune meeting a family's determined labour, though attributing the find to fate is the kural's frame, not the sources'.

1024.event_title: Vinoba Bhave receives an unasked-for gift of land at Pochampalli
1024.event: While walking through Telangana, Vinoba Bhave met landless Dalit families at Pochampalli who said they needed land to live. When he asked those present whether anything could be done, a landowner named Ramachandra Reddy rose and offered 100 acres, and from this unplanned beginning the Bhoodan (land-gift) movement grew, collecting millions of acres in later years.
1024.explanation: A movement of national scale began not from a plan but from a single spontaneous response during Vinoba's tireless walking tour.
1024.tie_back: The kural says that for those who strive without delay to raise their people, the work reaches its goal of itself even before it is planned, as the first land gift came to Vinoba unasked.
1024._accuracy_note: Closely matches the unplanned success the kural promises to prompt workers, applied to community rather than family.

1025.event_title: Robert Owen's New Lanark becomes a place of pilgrimage
1025.event: From 1800 Robert Owen managed the New Lanark cotton mills, where he shortened the working day, stopped children under ten from working in the mills, opened a nursery and infant school in 1816, and set up a village store selling good goods at fair prices. Paid for out of the mills' profits, these reforms drew visitors from many countries, and Britannica notes that the mills became a place of pilgrimage for political leaders, social reformers and royalty.
1025.explanation: Owen showed that a working community could be raised without exploitation, and the world came to see and learn from it.
1025.tie_back: The kural says the world gathers around the one who raises his people without fault, and New Lanark under Owen drew admirers from far and wide.
1025._accuracy_note: Fits the kural's reward of worldwide regard for blameless community-building, though Owen's 'family' here is his mill village rather than his kin.

1026.event_title: Young Andrew Carnegie works to keep his family afloat
1026.event: In 1848 the Carnegie family emigrated from Dunfermline, Scotland, to Allegheny, Pennsylvania, after mechanised looms ruined his father's handloom weaving. Young Andrew went straight to work as a bobbin boy in a cotton mill for $1.20 a week, then moved through better-paid jobs to the telegraph office; when his father died in 1855 he was the family's only breadwinner.
1026.explanation: Carnegie took charge of the household he was born into while still a boy, the start of a career that later made him one of the world's richest men.
1026.tie_back: The kural calls true manliness making oneself the leader and support of the family one was born into, which is what young Carnegie did.
1026._accuracy_note: Good illustration of a son taking up the burden of his birth family; his later fame rests on other things.

1027.event_title: The Widow Clicquot takes over her husband's wine firm
1027.event: When Francois Clicquot died in 1805, his 27-year-old widow Barbe-Nicole Clicquot Ponsardin persuaded her father-in-law to back her and took control of the family's wine business. She ran it through difficult wartime years, and the house dates her invention of the riddling table, a method of clearing sediment from champagne still in use, to 1816.
1027.explanation: A young widow with no business training carried the family firm and became one of the founders of the modern champagne industry.
1027.tie_back: The kural says that, as on the battlefield the load falls on the fearless, in a family it falls on those able to bear it, and the burden of the Clicquot house fell to Barbe-Nicole.
1027._accuracy_note: The burden-on-the-capable theme fits well; the battlefield half of the comparison is only figurative here.

1028.event_title: Maria Sklodowska works as a governess to put her sister through medical school
1028.place: Poland (then part of the Russian Empire)
1028.event: Young Maria Sklodowska, later Marie Curie, made an agreement with her elder sister Bronislawa that Maria would work first to pay for Bronya's medical studies in Paris, and Bronya would later help her in turn. Maria spent several years as a tutor and live-in governess, including a post with a family in the countryside north of Warsaw, before she was finally able to enrol at the Sorbonne in 1891.
1028.explanation: She put her own ambitions on hold and took humble work at once so that the family could advance, and the plan succeeded for both sisters.
1028.tie_back: The kural says that those who raise a family cannot wait for the right season or stand on their dignity, and Maria took modest work immediately rather than wait for better times.
1028._accuracy_note: A strong example of not waiting and not standing on dignity for the family's sake; the kural's warning of ruin is shown only by its avoidance.

1029.event_title: Dostoevsky takes on his late brother's family and debts
1029.event: When Fyodor Dostoevsky's brother and co-editor Mikhail died in 1864, Fyodor assumed financial responsibility for Mikhail's family and the debts of their journal Epoch, which collapsed in 1865. The years that followed were a time of acute financial hardship in which he wrote under heavy pressure and spent long periods abroad to escape creditors.
1029.explanation: Dostoevsky shouldered burdens that were not strictly his own, and they shaped years of his life and work.
1029.tie_back: The kural asks whether the body of one who shields his family from harm is only a vessel for suffering, and Dostoevsky's hard years carrying his brother's family are a vivid case.
1029._accuracy_note: Fits the image of a body bearing hardship to protect kin; his own gambling added to the hardship, so the suffering was not wholly for the family.

1030.event_title: The Medici are driven from Florence after Lorenzo's death
1030.event: Lorenzo de' Medici, who had steered Florence and his family's fortunes for over two decades, died in April 1492. His son Piero faced a French invasion under Charles VIII in 1494, made concessions to the French king that outraged the city, and was forced to flee as the Medici palace was sacked; he never saw Florence again.
1030.explanation: Without a capable leader to hold it up, a dominant family lost its power within two years when crisis came.
1030.tie_back: The kural warns that a family with no able person to prop it up falls like a tree when misfortune strikes its root, as the Medici house did in 1494.
1030._accuracy_note: A close illustration of a house falling when crisis struck and no strong hand held it up.
